summary.framework_finding: TDG's 10-K does not name any Pentagon Program Element, PE number, named program of record, or weapons platform. The defense narrative is delivered exclusively in aggregate ($3,761M FY25 / ~43% of revenue) with explicit emphasis on platform diversification (no customer >10%, top-10 ~40%, 90% proprietary across many platforms). The J-Book DIVERGENCE PATTERN requires a forward narrative load-bearing on a named program; TDG's filing is structurally immunized against this pattern by its components-supplier business model. NOT_FOUND in pentagon_jbook for contractor='TransDigm' across the 410-PE corpus, confirming TDG operates as a sub-tier supplier rather than a PE-named prime. USAspending shows the expected diffuse footprint: 2,491 DoD awards spread across subsidiaries (AeroControlex, Whippany Actuation Systems, Skurka Aerospace, etc.) with small per-award amounts and no PE concentration. This is a CLEAN result for this cohort's pattern — and a useful negative control: the J-Book divergence framework does not produce false positives on platform-diversified components suppliers.
